source.version: Harvard Business School Working Paper 24-013 / SSRN 4573321, dated September 22, 2023; working-paper number on PDF p. 1 and date on PDF p. 3 (printed p. 1). This is the saved working paper, not the later Organization Science version of record.
source.supplement_used: Appendices A-E in the same PDF, pp. 44-58: tasks, recommendation-quality rubric, retainment, collective variation, and Centaur/Cyborg practices. The raster rubric on PDF pp. 47-48 was also inspected visually.

studies.label: Inside-the-frontier experiment: creative footwear product innovation

counts_source.quote: Approximately half of the participants (385 consultants) tackled a series of tasks where they were prompted to conceptualize and develop new product ideas, focusing on aspects such as creativity, analytical skills, persuasiveness and writing skills.

arms.name: GPT Only
arms.description: Access to a company chat platform built on the OpenAI API and using GPT-4.

arms.name: GPT + Overview
arms.description: The same GPT-4 access plus a prompt-engineering overview with instructional videos and documents.

studies.country: Multinational; BCG offices around the world; individual countries not enumerated.
studies.task: Develop a new shoe for an underserved market, with ideas, prototype, product name, market segmentation, slogans, and launch communications across the experimental questions.

ai_tool.name: GPT-4, through a company OpenAI API platform resembling ChatGPT; end-of-April version with default system prompts and temperature.
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 12 (printed p. 8), Section 2, AI platform and model version

preregistration.where: OSF, https://osf.io/ytaev; described as embargoed and available from authors on request in PDF p. 9 (printed p. 5), Section 2 and footnote 2.

studies.label: Outside-the-frontier experiment: brand recommendation and tactical business ideas

counts_source.quote: The other half (373 consultants) engaged in business problem-solving tasks using quantitative data, customer and company interviews, and including a persuasive writing component.

arms.name: GPT Only
arms.description: Access to a company chat platform built on the OpenAI API and using GPT-4.

arms.name: GPT + Overview
arms.description: The same GPT-4 access plus a prompt-engineering overview with instructional videos and documents.

studies.country: Multinational; BCG offices around the world; individual countries not enumerated.
studies.task: Use company data and interviews to recommend a brand for investment and propose innovative tactical actions in a note to the CEO.

ai_tool.name: GPT-4, through a company OpenAI API platform resembling ChatGPT; end-of-April version with default system prompts and temperature.
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 12 (printed p. 8), Section 2, AI platform and model version

preregistration.where: OSF, https://osf.io/ytaev; described as embargoed and available from authors on request in PDF p. 9 (printed p. 5), Section 2 and footnote 2.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Mean of human grades across the 18 experimental questions, after averaging two graders for each answered question. Graders were BCG personnel or MBA students at a top program. The scale of this specific composite is not explicitly stated; it mixes creative product development, analysis, writing, and persuasion.

regression.model: Table 1, column (1). Unadjusted linear regression with both AI-arm indicators and Control as reference.

sources.locator: PDF p. 13 (printed p. 9), Outcome definition
sources.quote: Each response was evaluated by two human graders. We then calculated the mean grade assigned by humans to each question. This gave us 18 dependent variables (one per each question).

sources.locator: PDF p. 38 (printed p. 34), Table 1, column (1), Observations row (all arms)

estimates.notes: Printed full-model sample: 385 participants across all three arms. Per-arm counts and the total restricted to the two named arms are not printed, so n_treatment, n_control, and n_total remain null. This model shares its participants and outcome with the other specifications of the same contrast and is not an independent experiment. No outcome SD or standardized effect is reported. The paper calls response quality its primary outcome, but the preregistration was not available to verify primary status. This is a broad task-quality composite, not an isolated creativity rating. The regression coefficient is the treatment-versus-Control effect in the printed raw score units. Treatment-arm means and confidence intervals are not computed from it.

estimates.outcome: Quality of proposed tactical business actions
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Recommendation-quality rating on a 1-10 scale, assessed by two sets of human graders: BCG consultants and business-school students with grading experience. The Appendix B rubric assesses proposed tactical actions, strategic alignment, implementation detail, business reasoning, and anticipated profit impact.

estimates.notes: Printed full-model sample: 372 participants across all three arms. Per-arm counts and the total restricted to the two named arms are not printed, so n_treatment, n_control, and n_total remain null. This model shares its participants and outcome with the other specifications of the same contrast and is not an independent experiment. No outcome SD or standardized effect is reported. The quality analysis has fewer participants than the experiment-wide sample; no reason for the missing quality observation is given. The task requests innovative tactical actions, and the score assesses their usefulness. The regression coefficient is the treatment-versus-Control effect in the printed raw score units. Treatment-arm means and confidence intervals are not computed from it.

estimates.outcome: Between-participant semantic similarity of shoe ideas
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Google Universal Sentence Encoder represents each shoe idea as a 512-dimensional vector. The inner product of an idea with all ideas from other participants in the same arm is averaged first across those comparisons and then across the participant’s ideas. The resulting observation is a participant-level between-person similarity score; higher values mean more similar output.

sources.locator: PDF p. 52 (no printed page number), Outcome definition
sources.quote: More specifically, USE is designed to encode a piece of text into a 512-dimensional embedding vector that captures its underlying semantic meaning, in order to optimize transfer learning to downstream natural language processing tasks.

sources.locator: PDF p. 52 (no printed page number), Appendix D, Measuring Variation
sources.quote: We then compute the average inner-products between the idea of the given subject with all of the ideas produced by other subjects, within the same experimental condition.

sources.locator: PDF p. 53 (no printed page number), Appendix D, Results and Figure 1; also Figure 6 on PDF p. 36 (printed p. 32)
sources.quote: We consider the between semantic similarity measured for each subject, and plot its distribution and mean (with a vertical line) separately for each experimental condition in Figure 1.

estimates.notes: Only condition distributions and vertical mean lines are plotted; numeric arm means, SDs, SEs, intervals, tests, and analysis-specific participant counts are not printed. No figure values are estimated. The measure uses all other participants in the same condition, so participant scores share comparison data; no uncertainty estimator is described. Figure captions call it within-subject similarity, but the methods explicitly define between-subject similarity. The text reports reduced collective variation with AI access, without a quantified arm-specific effect.

sources.quote: We consider the between semantic similarity measured for each subject, and plot its distribution and mean (with a vertical line) separately for each experimental condition in Figure 1.

estimates.notes: Only condition distributions and vertical mean lines are plotted; numeric arm means, SDs, SEs, intervals, tests, and analysis-specific participant counts are not printed. No figure values are estimated. The measure uses all other participants in the same condition, so participant scores share comparison data; no uncertainty estimator is described. Figure captions call it within-subject similarity, but the methods explicitly define between-subject similarity. Both human AI configurations appear in the figure, but no numerical contrast or textual claim about their difference is reported.

open_items: The saved working paper predates the journal version of record. Changes to its results or supplements have not been checked against the journal text.

Arm-specific randomized and analyzed participant counts are not printed. Printed model totals include all arms, so pairwise n_total fields are null; model totals are preserved in notes and their sources. It is unclear which enrollment non-completers had been randomized.

The recommendation-quality analysis has a smaller full-model sample than the experiment-wide sample; the exclusion is not explained. Study-level counts follow the Methods, while model-specific totals follow the regression tables.

Participant-level outcome SDs and usable standardized effects are absent. Raw regression coefficients and robust SEs are retained without calculating standardizations, treatment means, or confidence intervals.

Semantic-similarity arm levels, uncertainty, and analysis-specific participant counts are not printed. Shared within-arm comparison pools create dependence whose treatment cannot be assessed without an uncertainty analysis.
The idea-list creativity result lacks a numerical table and an identified rater. Its measure is null rather than guessed; both AI arms are discussed together.
The preregistration is described as embargoed in this version. Its primary-outcome designation is not verified; paper-primary labels alone are not treated as preregistered-primary labels.

Brand-choice correctness is retained as convergent under extraction rule 6 despite its screening question being none. It is a right-answer analytic outcome and must remain outside pooled creativity effects.
Alternative full-sample regression specifications and pooled-AI summaries share observations with other estimates. Downstream selection must avoid treating them as independent evidence.
notes: The markdown was read from beginning to end, including all appendices. Every cited PDF page was checked with pymupdf text extraction; the raster recommendation rubric was additionally inspected without writing image files. Only printed numbers are recorded. The two experiments have separate participant samples (Section 2, PDF p. 10, printed p. 6); no overlap with other papers is identified in the screening form. Both use individual between-person randomization after an unassisted baseline, not a randomized-order crossover. Full-sample regression specifications are kept in separate, explicitly model-labeled records to preserve reported results; they are dependent estimates of the same contrasts. Printed trailing-zero precision is preserved in source quotes even where JSON numbers omit trailing zeros. No newer paper, posted data, or preregistration was retrieved.
